# Authorization and Access Control (AUTHZ)

Broken access control is the number one risk in the OWASP Top 10:2025. The server decides what each user may do; the app only reflects that decision.

## SCS-AUTHZ-01 Enforce role-based access control on the server for every feature

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Every feature and data access MUST be protected by role-based or claims-based authorization checked on the server, following least privilege. Users MUST only reach the functions and data their role needs. Client-side checks (hidden buttons, route guards, roles stored on the device) are for usability only and MUST NEVER be the only control.

Implementation (Flutter):

- Use go_router redirect or route guards to hide screens the user cannot use, but always expect the API to reject unauthorized calls.
- Never store the user's role or permissions on the device as the basis for a security decision.

Verification: Role matrix test: each role calls every endpoint, and unauthorized calls return 403.

## SCS-AUTHZ-03 Review application access rights and revoke them promptly

Level: MUST

Applies to: All (Flutter and Backend)

Policy: Application roles and access rights MUST be granted on approval, reviewed at least every six months for privileged roles and yearly for others, and removed promptly when a person leaves or changes role. Service accounts and API keys tied to a person MUST be rotated or disabled when that person leaves the team.

Implementation (all stacks):

- Prefer roles from Entra ID / AD groups, so leaving the company removes access automatically.
- For application-managed roles, provide an admin screen or report listing users and roles for the review.
- On a developer leaving: rotate any shared secrets they knew (Key Vault, SAP service passwords, signing keystore passwords), remove repository and pipeline access, and disable personal tokens.

Verification: Access review records; offboarding checklist completed for each leaver.
